note: The date period repair (#69). Unlike the previous round this is a real improvement and the category table shows why: `date` 7/15 -> 13/15, and every other category is byte-identical to the run before it. The +6 overall is exactly the date gain, with no collateral — which is what the #52/#59/#60 prompt attempts could never achieve.

previous.note: After the DISTINCT repair (#58), before the date repair (#69). `date` was 7/15.

known_failures.note: Nothing in the date category fails on every run any more. #58 and #69 are fixed deterministically; #59 and #60 remain open with a failed prompt attempt each on record (see PROJECT_STATUS.md). `group_by` and `having` are now the weakest categories, and both are dominated by cases already known to be non-deterministic rather than by a named defect.

always_failing.sales_cheapest_product: #59 — returns the measure, not the entity: SELECT MIN(price) instead of the product

known_failures.date_residue: emp_joined_2021 and sales_march_revenue each pass 2/3 rather than 0-1/3. Neither remaining failure is the #69 defect: one emits two comparisons with an invented upper bound (> '2020-12-31' AND <= '2021-03-15'), the other emits LIKE '%03-2024%', which is not a comparison at all. The repair correctly declines both. Fixing these means getting the model to stop inventing shapes, not widening a bound.

floor_rationale: Still 80, deliberately, despite 90.6. There is exactly ONE full round since #69, and raising a CI floor on a single sample of a measurement whose own recorded spread is ~5 points is how a gate starts flapping. `eval.yml` runs weekly — revisit once three or more post-#69 rounds exist, then set it ~6 points under the lowest. The floor's job is catching a category collapse, which 80 still does.
